raw_evidence.quote: The json type allows storing JSON objects.
The json and jsonb types allow creating columns for storing JSON objects.

The enum type allows storing a set of enumerated values.

raw_evidence.locator: §PostgreSQL (enum defined as a separate schema object, referenced via `type = enum.status`)

raw_evidence.quote: PostgreSQL has `uuid`, `bytea`, `inet`, `tsrange`; MySQL doesn't. SQL Server includes `money`, `smallmoney`, `nvarchar`, `identity`. ClickHouse features `IPv4`, `IPv6`, `FixedString`.

raw_evidence.locator: §PostgreSQL (domain with CHECK expression using Postgres-specific `~` regex operator and `VALUE` keyword)

product_neutrality_finding.rationale: The structural HCL keywords (`schema`, `table`, `column`, `primary_key`, `foreign_key`, `index`, `check`) are dialect-neutral and reused identically across every engine section observed. The dialect leak enters at the column-type and check-expression level, not the structural level: (1) type names diverge per engine — e.g. PostgreSQL-only `uuid`/`bytea`/`inet`, SQL-Server-only `money`/`nvarchar`, ClickHouse-only `IPv4`/`FixedString` — so a column's `type = ...` attribute is written differently per target database even when the intent (e.g. 'a JSON payload column') is the same; (2) the `enum` construct is not one construct but two incompatible ones — an inline `enum` type in MySQL versus a separately declared top-level `enum` schema object bound via `type = enum.<name>` in PostgreSQL — meaning an enum column's HCL differs by dialect, not just its emitted DDL; (3) the `check.expr` attribute holds a raw SQL boolean expression string in the target dialect's own syntax (the PostgreSQL domain example uses the Postgres-only `~` regex operator and the Postgres-only `VALUE` keyword), so any value constraint beyond type is authored in dialect SQL text embedded inside otherwise-neutral HCL, not in a dialect-neutral expression language. A schema author can keep table/column/key/index STRUCTURE product-neutral, but cannot keep TYPE NAMES, ENUM DECLARATION SHAPE, or CHECK EXPRESSION SYNTAX product-neutral once a dialect is chosen — the leak is real and appears at exactly the seams the brief's advanced constructs touch (json payload columns, enumerated domains, and the resource_task_weight value-constraint-beyond-type).

value_constraint_beyond_type_resource_ta.rationale: A constraint such as 'a decimal positive integer OR the literal ALL' can be written as a single `check { expr = "..." }` boolean SQL expression, per the documented `check` block mechanism. But `expr` is raw dialect SQL text (evidenced by the Postgres-specific `~`/`VALUE` syntax in the domain example), so the exact expression string is not portable across database engines without rewriting — hence workaround, not a native dialect-neutral value-constraint construct.
